summary: The bootstrap, upstream, scaffold PR, sync-back and hoist stages match their skill docs. The sync-down mechanics (3-way merge from the last synced commit, the no-base sidecar condition, .scaffold-keep skipping) are not described in skills/sync-scaffold.md; they live in bin/sync-from-scaffold.sh, so those claims have no support in the listed sources. The flow also omits that invoking /upstream is itself the merge authorization and when it stops at a ready PR.

code.overview: The downward half is real code: bin/bootstrap.sh installs the sync script and bin/sync-from-scaffold.sh does the manifest read, 3-way merge, sidecars, keep list and SHA bookkeeping, with an optional workflow that runs it and opens a PR. The upward half (/upstream) is agent-followed prose; code only enforces its edges, through the manifest checks in scripts/resolver-phases.ts and the CI jobs. /hoist-skill is implemented in tools/hoist-skill/.

refs.title: bootstrap: add the remote and install the sync script
refs.explain: It adds a git remote named scaffold if there is none and fetches its main branch. It creates bin/ and writes the sync script from scaffold/main using `git show`. It marks the script executable.
refs.why: This is all the first-time curl does to the repo: one new script, no tracked file changed. Later syncs need only git.

refs.anchor: echo "Or re-run bootstrap with --run to sync immediately:"
refs.title: bootstrap: run the sync only when asked
refs.explain: If --run was passed it runs the sync script at once. Otherwise it prints that setup is complete and shows the command for the first sync. It also mentions the optional workflow install.
refs.why: The first sync waits for the user to confirm. By default the script stops after installing, so nothing is merged into the project unasked.

refs.anchor: echo "error: could not read manifest .github/scaffold-files.txt from scaffold/main" >&2
refs.title: Read the manifest from scaffold/main
refs.explain: It reads .github/scaffold-files.txt from the fetched scaffold/main. If that read fails it prints an error and exits before any write. It then loads each non-empty line into the list of files to sync.
refs.why: The manifest decides which files scaffold ships. Aborting on a failed read stops an empty list from being recorded as a successful sync.

refs.anchor: # Returns 0 if $1 matches any pattern in .scaffold-keep, 1 otherwise.
refs.title: in_keep_list: match a path against .scaffold-keep
refs.explain: It returns 'no match' when the repo has no .scaffold-keep file. Otherwise it reads the file line by line, skipping blank lines and comments. It returns a match as soon as the path fits one pattern as a shell glob.
refs.why: Paths the project owns are skipped on every sync, even new ones. Without this a sync would overwrite files the project chose to keep.

refs.title: sync_file: 3-way merge, or a sidecar when there is no base
refs.explain: When a last synced SHA exists and had this file, it writes three temp copies: the local file, the file at the last SHA, and the file on scaffold/main. `git merge-file` merges them; a clean result replaces the file, a conflict writes the marked-up result and records the file as a conflict. With no base, the incoming copy is written to <file>.scaffold-new and the original is left alone.
refs.why: This is the core of sync down. The base makes local edits survive a merge; the sidecar avoids a silent first-sync overwrite.

refs.title: Save the synced SHA only on a clean sync
refs.explain: After all files are processed it checks three things: this is not a dry run, there are no conflicts, and there are no sidecars pending review. Only then does it write scaffold's commit SHA to .github/scaffold-sync-sha.
refs.why: The saved SHA is the merge base for the next sync. Holding it back while conflicts or sidecars remain means a re-run still sees the unfinished files.

refs.anchor: --body "Automated sync from [victusfate/scaffold](https://github.com/victusfate/scaffold). Review the diff before merging — any conflicts have markers and need manual resolution." \
refs.title: Workflow: run the sync and open a PR
refs.explain: On manual dispatch the job runs the sync script and records whether the tree changed. If it did, it commits everything on a branch named chore/sync-scaffold-guidance and pushes it. It opens a PR unless one for that branch is already open.
refs.why: This is the optional hands-off form of sync down, installed by bootstrap --with-workflow. It still lands through a PR, so a person reviews the diff.

refs.anchor: export function phaseScaffold(rows: ResolverRow[], { fail, warn, MANIFEST, listedInManifest, rel }: PhaseCtx): void {
refs.title: phaseScaffold: every skill path must be in the manifest
refs.explain: It fails if the manifest file is missing. For each row in the skill resolver table it fails when the skill's path is not listed in the manifest. It warns if the resolver table or the check script itself is not listed.
refs.why: The 'scaffold way' includes adding new files to the manifest. Without this check a new skill could merge into scaffold and never reach a consumer.

refs.anchor: fail('Manifest', `${files.length} tracked files under ${top} are neither shipped nor held back — add \`${top}\` to ${rel(INTERNAL)} to hold back the directory, or list each file in ${rel(MANIFEST)}`);
refs.title: phaseManifestCompleteness: every tracked file is shipped or held back
refs.explain: It runs only in scaffold, where the internal list exists. Every tracked file that is in neither the manifest nor the internal list is an error. Every manifest entry that is not tracked, or is also internal, is an error.
refs.why: A script or tool added upstream must be classified before the gates pass. This closes the 'added a file but forgot the manifest' gap.

refs.anchor: "test:checks": "node scripts/check-resolvable.ts --strict && node scripts/update-skills-doc.ts --check && node scripts/check-agents-detail.ts && node scripts/check-handoff.ts && node scripts/check-guidelines.ts && node scripts/render-explorer-pages.ts --check && node scripts/render-diagrams.ts --check",
refs.title: The gates /upstream runs locally
refs.explain: `test` chains the node tests, tool tests, shell tests and the check scripts. `test:checks` starts with `check-resolvable.ts --strict` and the skills-doc freshness check. `lint` is eslint with zero warnings allowed and `typecheck` is `tsc --noEmit`.
refs.why: These are the three commands the upstream step requires before pushing. The resolver and manifest checks above run inside `npm test`.

refs.title: CI lint job on the scaffold PR
refs.explain: On a pull request to main the job installs dependencies, then runs lint, typecheck and the import-boundary check. The verify job in the same file runs `npm test`.
refs.why: These are the real checks whose conclusions must be read before merging the scaffold PR. Writing the PR body and deciding whether the merge is authorized are left to the agent.

refs.anchor: echo "error: --mark-resolved needs a committed, marker-free managed file: $file" >&2
refs.title: --mark-resolved: accept a committed conflict resolution
refs.explain: For each file passed with --mark-resolved it checks that the file is in the manifest, exists, is tracked, has no unstaged or staged changes, and contains no conflict markers. Any failure prints an error and exits before the sync writes anything.
refs.why: After resolving a diverged file the re-run must accept the project's version instead of merging again. The checks stop a file being marked resolved while markers or uncommitted edits remain.

refs.anchor: elif [ -f AGENTS.md ] && { ! git diff --quiet -- AGENTS.md || ! git diff --cached --quiet -- AGENTS.md; }; then
refs.title: Compose AGENTS.md from scaffold's copy plus AGENTS.local.md
refs.explain: When AGENTS.local.md exists, AGENTS.md is skipped if it is on the keep list or has uncommitted edits. Otherwise the script takes scaffold's AGENTS.md and appends a marked block holding AGENTS.local.md. It writes the result only if it differs.
refs.why: This is one coded place for the project-specific half of a rule: it lives in AGENTS.local.md and is re-attached on every sync. The upstream text stays identical to scaffold's.

refs.anchor: let header = '# .sync/hoisted — skills hoisted from scaffold; replayed by /pull-scaffold.\n# <name>\t<harness>\t<ref>\n';
refs.title: upsertManifest: record hoisted skills in .sync/hoisted
refs.explain: It reads the existing entries and keeps the file's comment header. For each new entry it replaces the one with the same name and harness, or appends it. It writes one tab-separated line per entry: name, harness, ref.
refs.why: This is the /hoist-skill record of what was exported and at which pinned ref. Without it a later replay would not know which skills to re-emit.
